integrity: The proof uses only the defining [k]-Roman inequality, the two leaf-support pairs of the half graph, and the nested neighborhoods of the first interior vertices. Each leaf-support pair has weight at least k; if one has weight exactly k, the zero support forces extra active excess and hence a global lower bound of 2(k+1). At equality, an endpoint pair of weight k leads to a direct interior-vertex contradiction. Thus both endpoint pairs have weight k+1 and all interior labels vanish; the zero vertices a_2 and b_{n-1} then force the two universal endpoints to carry k+1.
scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes k at least two and n at least three; the excluded boundary cases have additional minimum functions.
The scalar k=2 value is already implied by the published double-Roman theorem for connected chain graphs and is not an originality basis.
Only minimum functions are classified; higher-weight feasible labelings are not enumerated.
Finite verification covers k from two through five and n from three through five and is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed optimizer classification may exist.
title: Unique minimum \([k]\)-Roman functions of half graphs
